# Judith Chapter 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_014_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And Judith said to them, "Hear me now, my brothers: take this head and hang it on the parapet of your wall.

**2** And it will be, when morning appears and the sun comes up on the earth, each one of you shall take up his weapons of war and every able-bodied man shall go out of the city, and you shall set a captain over them as if you were going down to the plain against the advance guard of the Assyrian forces — but do not go down.

**3** And they will take up their arms and go to their camp and rouse the commanders of the Assyrian army, and they will run to the tent of Holofernes and not find him. And fear will fall upon them and they will flee before your face.

**4** And you and all who inhabit every territory of Israel will pursue them and cut them down in their paths.

**5** But before you do these things, summon to me Achior the Ammonite, so that he may see and recognize the one who treated the house of Israel with contempt and who sent him to us as if to his death."

**6** And they summoned Achior from the house of Uzziah. When he came and saw the head of Holofernes in the hand of one of the men in the assembly of the people, he fell on his face and his spirit left him.

**7** And when they raised him up, he fell at the feet of Judith and bowed down before her face, and said, "Blessed are you in every tent of Judah, and in every nation, those who hear your name will be dismayed.

**8** And now tell me all the things you did in these days." And Judith told him all the things she had done, in the presence of all the people. And when she finished speaking, the people shouted aloud and made a joyful noise in their city.

**9** And when Achior saw all the things that the God of Israel had done, he believed strongly in God and had himself circumcised in his flesh, and he was added to the house of Israel, even to this day.

**10** And as soon as the morning appeared, they hung the head of Holofernes on the wall, and every man took up his weapons, and they went out in companies to the ascents of the mountain.

**11** And when the Assyrians saw them, they sent word to their commanders, and those went to the generals and the captains and to every ruler.

**12** And they came to the tent of Holofernes and said to the one who managed all his affairs, "Wake up our master, for the slaves have dared to come down against us for battle — to their utter destruction."

**13** And Bagoas went in and knocked at the door of the tent, for he supposed he was sleeping with Judith.

**14** And when no one answered, he opened and went into the bedchamber and found him thrown on the threshold, dead, with his head taken from him.

**15** And he cried out with a loud voice and wept and groaned and shouted and tore his garments.

**16** And he entered the tent where Judith had lodged and did not find her; and he rushed out to the people and cried,

**17** "The slaves have been treacherous! One Hebrew woman has brought disgrace upon the house of King Nebuchadnezzar! For behold, Holofernes is on the ground, and his head is not on him!"

**18** And when the commanders of the Assyrian army heard these words, they tore their garments and an excessive distress fell upon them, and there arose in their camp a cry and a very great shouting.

**19** And the men in the tents, when they heard it, were astounded at what had happened.

---
*EMET notes: v. 6 — "his spirit left him" (exepsychē) — literally "his soul/spirit went out," a common Greek idiom for fainting/shock rather than death, though the word is used for actual death in other contexts. v. 9 — "believed strongly in God" renders episteuse sphodra — intensive belief. v. 13 — "he supposed he was sleeping with Judith" — the irony is devastating. v. 14 — "thrown on the threshold" — not in his bed but on the floor, in the posture of a discarded thing.*
